title: Rejection, Sending of the Twelve, and Miracles

questions.question: When Jesus returned to His hometown of Nazareth, what specifically did many of the people ask in astonishment when He taught in the synagogue?
options: "Is not this the carpenter, the son of Mary?"
"Is he not the son of Joseph the stonemason?"
"Has he not learned from the Pharisees?"
"Where did he find such holy scrolls?"
questions.correctAnswer: "Is not this the carpenter, the son of Mary?"
questions.explanation: Mark 6:3 (ESV): "Is not this the carpenter, the son of Mary and brother of James and Joses and Judas and Simon? And are not his sisters here with us?"

questions.question: Because of their unbelief in Nazareth, what could Jesus not do there?
options: He could do no mighty work there, except laying His hands on a few sick people and healing them
He could not speak a single word because they silenced Him
He could not enter the synagogue at all
He could not gather any disciples from that town
questions.correctAnswer: He could do no mighty work there, except laying His hands on a few sick people and healing them
questions.explanation: Mark 6:5 (ESV): "And he could do no mighty work there, except that he laid his hands on a few sick people and healed them."

questions.question: When Jesus called the twelve and began to send them out two by two, what did He charge them to take for their journey?
options: Nothing except a staff—no bread, no bag, no money in their belts
Only enough bread for one week
A sword for protection and two tunics
A scroll of the scriptures to read from
questions.correctAnswer: Nothing except a staff—no bread, no bag, no money in their belts
questions.explanation: Mark 6:8 (ESV): "He charged them to take nothing for their journey except a staff—no bread, no bag, no money in their belts—"

questions.question: If any place will not receive or listen to the twelve, what were they instructed to do when leaving?
options: Shake off the dust that is on your feet as a testimony against them
Curse the town in the name of the Lord
Cry out in the streets that judgment is coming
Refuse to ever speak to a person from that town again
questions.correctAnswer: Shake off the dust that is on your feet as a testimony against them
questions.explanation: Mark 6:11 (ESV): "And if any place will not receive you and they will not listen to you, when you leave, shake off the dust that is on your feet as a testimony against them."

questions.question: When King Herod heard about Jesus, who did he believe Jesus was, since he said, "He has been raised from the dead"?
options: John the Baptist
Elijah
King David
One of the prophets of old
questions.explanation: Mark 6:16 (ESV): "But when Herod heard of it, he said, 'John, whom I beheaded, has been raised.'"

questions.question: Herodias wanted to put John the Baptist to death because John had told Herod what was not lawful?
options: "It is not lawful for you to have your brother's wife."
"It is not lawful for you to collect taxes from God's people."
"It is not lawful for you to build temples to foreign gods."
"It is not lawful to associate with Romans."
questions.correctAnswer: "It is not lawful for you to have your brother's wife."
questions.explanation: Mark 6:18 (ESV): "For John had been saying to Herod, 'It is not lawful for you to have your brother's wife.'"

questions.question: Herod feared John the Baptist because he knew John was a righteous and holy man, so Herod did what?
options: He kept him safe
He made him a counselor
He offered him all the wealth he desired
He released him immediately
questions.explanation: Mark 6:20 (ESV): "for Herod feared John, knowing that he was a righteous and holy man, and he kept him safe..."

questions.question: What prompted Herod to swear to give Herodias' daughter whatever she asked, up to half his kingdom?
options: She came in and danced, pleasing Herod and his guests
She saved his life from an assassin
She accurately foretold a great victory
She sang a lament that moved him to tears
questions.correctAnswer: She came in and danced, pleasing Herod and his guests
questions.explanation: Mark 6:22 (ESV): "For when Herodias's daughter came in and danced, she pleased Herod and his guests..."

questions.question: Why did the disciples suggest Jesus send the crowd away in the desolate place?
options: So they could go into the surrounding region and buy themselves something to eat
So Jesus could rest from his teaching
Because the Romans were approaching
Because a storm was beginning to gather
questions.correctAnswer: So they could go into the surrounding region and buy themselves something to eat
questions.explanation: Mark 6:35-36 (ESV): "...This is a desolate place, and the hour is now late. Send them away to go into the surrounding country and villages and buy themselves something to eat."

questions.question: In the feeding of the five thousand, how many loaves and fish did they find?
options: Five loaves and two fish
Seven loaves and a few small fish
Two loaves and five fish
Three loaves and a large fish
questions.explanation: Mark 6:38 (ESV): "And he said to them, 'How many loaves do you have? Go and see.' And when they had found out, they said, 'Five, and two fish.'"

questions.question: After everyone ate and was satisfied, how many baskets full of broken pieces and fish were taken up?
options: Twelve baskets full
Seven baskets full
Forty baskets full
Three baskets full
questions.explanation: Mark 6:43 (ESV): "And they took up twelve baskets full of broken pieces and of the fish."

questions.question: Later that night, the disciples were struggling to row into the wind. About the fourth watch of the night, Jesus came to them walking on the sea, and meant to do what?
options: He meant to pass by them
He meant to overturn their boat as a lesson
He meant to guide them with a lantern
He meant to show them where the fish were
questions.correctAnswer: He meant to pass by them
questions.explanation: Mark 6:48 (ESV): "And about the fourth watch of the night he came to them, walking on the sea. He meant to pass by them,"

questions.question: When the disciples saw Him walking on the sea, they were terrified. What did Jesus say to them?
options: "Take heart; it is I. Do not be afraid."
"Why are you fearful, O you of little faith?"
"Look upon the Son of God!"
"Do you not recognize your Master?"
questions.correctAnswer: "Take heart; it is I. Do not be afraid."
questions.explanation: Mark 6:50 (ESV): "...But immediately he spoke to them and said, 'Take heart; it is I. Do not be afraid.'"

questions.question: Why were the disciples utterly astounded when Jesus got into the boat and the wind ceased?
options: For they did not understand about the loaves, but their hearts were hardened
Because they had never seen a storm end so quickly
For they believed He was just a prophet
Because they thought he intended to walk all the way to shore
questions.correctAnswer: For they did not understand about the loaves, but their hearts were hardened
questions.explanation: Mark 6:52 (ESV): "for they did not understand about the loaves, but their hearts were hardened."

questions.question: When Jesus arrived at Gennesaret, the people laid the sick in the marketplaces and implored Him that they might touch what?
options: Even the fringe of his garment
His shadow as it passed by
The sandals on his feet
The staff in his hand
questions.correctAnswer: Even the fringe of his garment
questions.explanation: Mark 6:56 (ESV): "they laid the sick in the marketplaces and implored him that they might touch even the fringe of his garment. And as many as touched it were made well."

key_verse_text: for they all saw him and were terrified. But immediately he spoke to them and said, "Take heart; it is I. Do not be afraid."
